Rule/Concept: Nouns with Two Parts (Plural in Form and Function) Certain nouns in English describe items that are made of two parts working together. These nouns are always treated as plural and require a plural verb. Even though "scissors" refers to a single tool, grammatically it is not a singular entity.

These nouns are always used as plural: Scissors, Pliers, Tweezers, Tongs, Shears, Spectacles, Glasses, Pants, Jeans, Trousers, Shorts, Leggings, Binoculars etc..

Corrected Sentence: The scissors are on the table.

Things to Remember/Exam Tips

The "Pair" Shift: If these nouns are preceded by the phrase "A pair of," the subject becomes singular because you are now referring to the "pair".

Example: "A pair of scissors is on the table."

Context is King: In competitive exams, look for the presence of "pair." If "pair" is missing, treat words like scissors, pants, and binoculars as plural.

Visual Check: If the object has two "legs" or "blades" that can be separated but function as one, it is almost certainly plural.

A group of students _______ studying in the library.

The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns with Indefinite Articles Changing "The" to "A" does not change the fundamental rule of subject-verb agreement for collective nouns. Whether it is "The group" or "A group," the word "group" remains a singular collective noun representing one single unit.

Subject Focus: The subject is "group" (singular), not "students" (plural). The phrase "of students" is simply providing more information about the group.

Common Phrases following this rule: A pack of wolves is, A bunch of keys is, A team of players is, A fleet of ships is.

Correct Sentence: A group of students is studying in the library.

questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

A number of students _______ participating in the annual sports meet.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- Replace the blank with "are".

Rule/Concept: "A Number of" vs. "The Number of" This is a high-frequency exception in competitive exams. Unlike "A group of," the phrase "A number of" functions as a plural quantifier (meaning "many" or "several"). Therefore, it always takes a plural verb.

Why it is Plural:

A number of: This phrase is used to mean "some" or "many." The focus is on the individual students within the group, making the subject plural.

The number of: This phrase refers to the specific total or the numerical value itself (e.g., "The number of students is 50"). Since a "total" is a single figure, it takes a singular verb.

Examples:

A number of workers have gone on strike. (Plural)

The number of workers on strike is twenty. (Singular)

Corrected Sentence: A number of students are participating in the annual sports meet.

Rule/Concept: The Proximity Rule (Neither/Nor) In sentences using "neither... nor", the verb must agree with the subject that is physically closer to it in the sentence. The first subject mentioned has no effect on the verb form.

Things to Remember/Exam Tips

The "Nor" Anchor: Always draw a line after the word "nor." Everything before that line is irrelevant to the verb. Only look at the noun after the line.

Don't "Balance" the Sentence: Many students think that if one subject is plural, the verb should be plural to "cover" everyone. This is a trap. Only the closest neighbour matters.

The S-Rule: Remember that for most verbs in the present tense, adding an -s makes it singular (Rutu wants), while removing the -s makes it plural (Classmates want).

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The group of players _______ arriving at the stadium for the final match tomorrow.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C). Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns and Future Arrangements A collective noun (like group) refers to multiple people acting as a single unit. Even when the sentence refers to a future event (indicated by "tomorrow"), we use the Present Continuous tense ("is arriving") to describe a fixed plan or arrangement.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: The subject is "The group" (singular). The word "players" is part of the prepositional phrase "of players" and does not influence the verb.

The "Tomorrow" Factor: In English, the present continuous (is/are + verb-ing) is commonly used to talk about scheduled future actions.

Why (D) "was" is incorrect: "Was" is a singular past tense verb. While it matches the singular subject "group," it contradicts the word "tomorrow," which requires a present or future tense.

Why (B) "are" is incorrect: "Are" is plural. It would only be correct if the subject was "The players," but here the subject is the singular "group."

The Three Musketeers _______ often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The Three Musketeers _______ often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B). Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Titles as Abstract Singular Entities:

In English, names of books, movies, countries, or organizations are treated as singular proper nouns. Even if the title contains a plural noun (Musketeers) or a number (Three), it represents one single entity (one story).

The "Article A" Anchor: In complex sentences, look for the phrase "a prime example." The use of the singular article "a" later in the sentence is a dead giveaway that the subject must be singular.

Proper Noun Identification: Words that are capitalized in the middle of a sentence (The Three Musketeers) are usually titles. Treat them as a single "IT," not "THEY."

Common Traps: Watch out for similar titles like Gulliver's Travels, Hard Times, The Arabian Nights, or The United Nations. All of these take a singular verb.

Elimination Strategy: If you see a singular complement (like "a prime example"), immediately eliminate all plural verb options.

Why "Was" (Option C) is incorrect here: If you choose "was," you are implying that the book used to be cited as an example in the past, but it is no longer considered one today. Since the literary status of a masterpiece is usually a continuous fact, the present tense "is" is the grammatically superior choice.

Adverbs of Frequency: Words like "often," "usually," "generally," and "always" are strong signals that the examiner is testing you on the Simple Present Tense.

Correct Sentence: The Three Musketeers is often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C). Both "All is well" and "All are well" are grammatically correct, but they carry different meanings based on the context.

Rule/Concept: "All" as an Indefinite Pronoun The word "All" is treated as singular when it refers to a non-countable concept or a general situation. It is treated as plural when it refers to countable people or things.

Logic Breakdown:

"All is well" (Option A): In this case, "All" refers to a general condition, state of affairs, or everything as a whole (Uncountable).

Example: Everything in life is going fine. (All is well).

"All are well" (Option B): Here, "All" refers to specific individuals or members of a group, such as family members or friends (Countable).

Example: All the people in my family are doing fine. (All are well).

In a society where corruption and greed often seem to dominate the headlines, it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest _______ rewarded for their integrity.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

In a society where corruption and greed often seem to dominate the headlines, it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest _______ rewarded for their integrity.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (A)- The blank should be filled with the plural verb "are".

Rule/Concept: Adjectives Used as Nouns (The + Adjective) In English grammar, when the definite article "the" is placed before an adjective (like honest, poor, rich, blind, young, dead), the phrase functions as a plural noun. It refers to a whole group or class of people. Because it represents a group of individuals, it always takes a plural verb.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "The honest" does not mean one honest person; it means "honest people in general."

Why (C) is incorrect: "Is" is singular. While "honesty" (the abstract noun) takes a singular verb, "the honest" (the group of people) requires a plural verb.

Correct Sentence: ...it is heartening to observe that ultimately the honest are rewarded for their integrity.

Tips:

The Group Rule: Always remember the formula: The + Adjective = Plural People.

The poor are... (Poor people)

The rich are... (Rich people)

The unemployed are... (Unemployed people)

Noun vs. Adjective: Do not confuse "The honest" with "Honesty."

Honesty is the best policy. (Abstract noun = Singular)

The honest are respected. (Group of people = Plural)

Rule 1: The + Adjective (Collective Noun) When the definite article "the" is used with an adjective (like poor, rich, brave, honest), it represents a whole class of people and is always plural.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Ninety percent of the students _______ the examination this year.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B)- The blank should be filled with the plural present perfect verb "have passed".

Rule/Concept: Fractions and Percentages (The "Of" Rule) When a sentence starts with a percentage (e.g., 90%), a fraction (e.g., one-third), or a portion (e.g., some, all, most), the verb agrees with the noun following the word "of".

Logic Breakdown:

The Noun after "of": In this sentence, the noun is "students" (Plural Countable Noun).

Verb Agreement: Since "students" is plural, the verb must also be plural.

Tense Choice: The phrase "this year" often suggests an action that has recently been completed, making the Present Perfect ("have passed") the most appropriate choice over the simple past in many exam contexts.

Correct Sentence: Something like ninety percent of the students have passed the examination this year.

questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

During the annual cultural festival held at the university last year, every boy and every girl _______ present to witness the spectacular performance.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C)- The blank should be filled with the singular past tense verb "was".

Rule 1: The "Each/Every" Rule (Subject-Verb Agreement) Even when multiple nouns are joined by "and," if they are preceded by "each" or "every," the entire subject is treated as singular. This is because the focus is on every individual person separately.

Incorrect: Every boy and girl were...

Correct: Every boy and girl was/is...

Rule 2: Tense Consistency (Time Markers) In competitive exams, once you identify the subject is singular, you must check the time marker to choose between "is" and "was."

The sentence contains the phrase "last year."

"Last year" indicates a completed action in the past (Simple Past Tense).

Therefore, the singular present verb "is" is incorrect, and the singular past verb "was" must be used.

Correct Sentence: ...every boy and every girl was present to witness the spectacular performance.

questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Boy and girl each _______ present at the venue today to participate in the seminar.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)- The blank should be filled with the plural present tense verb "are"

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "Boy and girl" joined by "and" creates a plural subject.

The Position of "Each": Because "each" appears after the nouns, the plural agreement is maintained.

Tense Consistency: The word "today" indicates the Present Tense.

Why (B) "is" is incorrect: While "is" is present tense, it is singular. The placement of "each" after the subject prevents the sentence from becoming singular.

Why (A) and (C) are eliminated: Both "was" and "were" are past tense forms and contradict the current time marker "today."

Correct Sentence: Boy and girl each are present at the venue today...

The "Each" Location Check:

Before Subject: 1.Each boy and girl is...

Before Subject: 2.Each boy and each girl is…

After Subject: Boy and girl each are...

The technician noticed that one of the _______ in the laboratory _______ malfunctioning at the moment.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The technician noticed that one of the _______ in the laboratory _______ malfunctioning at the moment.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D).

The blanks should be filled with "equipment" and "is".

Rule 1: The Uncountable Noun Trap In English, certain nouns are "uncountable" and never take an "s," even when referring to multiple items. Equipment is one of the most common words tested. Even after the phrase "one of the," you cannot say "equipments".

Incorrect: One of the equipments...

Correct: One of the equipment...

Rule 2: "One of" Subject-Verb Agreement The true subject of the sentence is the word "One," not the noun that follows the word "of". Therefore, the verb must be singular to agree with "One".

Logic: One (Singular Subject) + is (Singular Verb).

Why the other options are confusing:

Option (B) [equipment / are]: This uses the correct noun form but incorrectly uses the plural verb "are" to match the mental idea of "many pieces of equipment." However, grammar requires agreement with the word "One".

Correct Sentence: ...one of the equipment in the laboratory is malfunctioning at the moment.

The "No-S" List (Uncountable Nouns)

These nouns are always considered singular and never take an "s," even when they refer to a large quantity.

Category

Nouns that NEVER take "s"

Material/Items

Equipment, Furniture, Luggage, Baggage, Jewellery, Pottery

Abstract/Ideas

Information, Advice, Knowledge, Evidence, Work, Progress

Generalizations

Scenery, Poetry, Machinery, Stationery, Fuel

Food/Materials

Bread, Butter, Food, Paper, Wood, Iron

Rule/Concept: Single Article = Single Person

the number of articles determines the number of people. When two titles (like monitor and captain) are joined by "and," but only the first title has an article (The), it means the same person is performing both roles.

Logic Breakdown:

Verb Agreement: Since the subject is singular, the singular verb "is" in segment (C) is perfectly correct.

The "Two-Person" Trap: If the sentence were about two different people, it would have been: "The monitor and the captain are..." Since the second "the" is missing, we must treat it as one person.

questions.q_en: Select the sentence that is grammatically incorrect.
questions.q_hi: Select the sentence that is grammatically incorrect.
options_en: The poet and dramatist has been honored with the Sahitya Academy Award this year.
More than one student has successfully cleared the preliminary round of the exam.
Five miles are a long distance to cover on foot for an elderly person.
None of the information provided by the witness was found to be reliable.
options_hi: The poet and dramatist has been honored with the Sahitya Academy Award this year.
More than one student has successfully cleared the preliminary round of the exam.
Five miles are a long distance to cover on foot for an elderly person.
None of the information provided by the witness was found to be reliable.
questions.solution_en:
The answer it Option (C)- as it remains the incorrect sentence. The plural verb "are" should be replaced with the singular verb "is."

Rule 1 (The Primary Error): Units of Measurement When a plural noun (like miles, rupees, or liters) represents a specific distance, amount, or weight being treated as a single unit, the verb must be singular.

Incorrect: Five miles are a long distance...

Correct: Five miles is a long distance...

Why the other sentences are CORRECT (The Traps)

Why option (A) is correct: One Article Rule

"The poet and dramatist" uses only one article ("The") before the first noun.

This means one person is both a poet and a dramatist.

Therefore, the singular verb "has" is perfectly correct.



Why option (B) is correct: The "More than one" Rule

Although "More than one" sounds plural, it is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.

"More than one student (singular) has (singular)..." is grammatically correct in formal English exams.

Why Option (C) is Correct: The "None of" + Uncountable Rule

In this sentence, "information" is an uncountable noun

When "None of" is followed by an uncountable noun, the verb must be singular.

Correct Sentence: Five miles is a long distance to cover on foot for an elderly person.

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.solution_en:
The error lies in option (A)- The singular verb "was" must be replaced with the plural verb "were."

Rule/Concept: Collective Nouns (Division of Opinion) Normally, a collective noun (like jury, committee, team, family) takes a singular verb when the group acts as one unit. However, if the members are divided, have different opinions, or are acting individually, the noun is treated as plural.

Logic Breakdown:

The "Division" Clue: Segment (B) uses the word "divided" and segment (C) uses "opinions" (plural). This proves the members are not acting as a single unit.

The Pronoun Clue: Segment (B) uses the plural possessive pronoun "their." A singular subject ("was") cannot be paired with a plural pronoun ("their") in the same sentence.

The Conflict: To maintain consistency with "divided" and "their," the verb in segment (A) must be plural (were).

Corrected Sentence: The jury were divided in their opinions regarding the verdict.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

'The members of the committee each _______ a different opinion regarding the new policy last week.'
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (C)

The blank should be filled with the singular past tense verb "had".

Rule/Concept: Post-Subject

when the word "each" follows a plural subject (like "The members" or "Boy and girl"), it does not change the plural nature of the subject. Therefore, the verb must remain plural.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "The members" is a plural subject.

The Position of "Each": Because "each" is placed after the plural subject, the verb must stay plural.

Tense Consistency: The phrase "last week" indicates a past action. In English, "had" serves as the past tense form for both singular and plural subjects.

Why (A) and (D) are incorrect: Both "has" and "was" are strictly singular verbs. Since "each" is after the subject, the sentence requires plural agreement.

Why (B) is incorrect: "Have" is the plural present form. It is incorrect here because it contradicts the past time marker "last week."

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

He is one of our _______ who _______ always been ready to sacrifice their personal interests for the welfare of the organization.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D)

The blanks should be filled with "employees" and "have".

Rule 1: "One of our" + Plural Noun The phrase "one of our" implies a selection from a group. Therefore, the noun following it must be plural.

Correct: One of our employees.

Rule 2: Relative Pronoun (Who) Agreement When a relative pronoun (who, which, that) is used, the verb that follows it must agree with the antecedent (the noun immediately before "who"). In this structure, the antecedent is the plural noun "employees," not the singular "He" or "One".

Logic: ...employees (Plural Antecedent) + who + have (Plural Verb).

Correct Sentence: He is one of our employees who have always been ready...

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: sold in this grocery store
are of very poor quality.
options_hi: sold in this grocery store
are of very poor quality.
questions.solution_en:
The error lies in option (A)- It should be "The bread and the butter."

Rule/Concept: Separate Entities vs. A Single Unit When "bread" and "butter" are being discussed as separate commodities being sold or bought (acting differently), they must each have their own article (The). Because there are two distinct items, the sentence then requires a plural verb.

Logic Breakdown:

Often Confused: Students often remember "Bread and butter is my favourite breakfast." This is correct because it's one meal.

The Conflict: In this sentence, the context is a "grocery store." A store sells bread as one item and butter as another separate item.

The Error: Because they are separate products, option (A) must have a second "the" to show plurality.

Corrected Sentence: The bread and the butter sold in this grocery store are of very poor quality.

questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The optician mentioned that a new pair of _______ _______ been kept aside for the customer who visited the shop yesterday.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B). The blanks should be filled with "spectacles" and "has".

Rule 1: Naturally Plural Nouns Nouns that consist of two symmetrical parts (like spectacles, scissors, pants, binoculars) are always used in the plural form. There is no such word as "spectacle" when referring to eyewear; "spectacle" (singular) actually means a "grand sight or scene."

Incorrect: A pair of spectacle

Correct: A pair of spectacles

Rule 2: The "A Pair of" Singular Agreement When you use the phrase "A pair of," the word "pair" becomes the head noun (subject) of the sentence. Since "a pair" is singular, it requires a singular verb.

Exam-Focused Tips:

The Suffix Trap: Never remove the 's' from spectacles, scissors, or trousers just because "a pair" is singular. The noun stays plural, but the verb turns singular.

Subject Identification: If "pair" is missing, use a plural verb (are, were, have). If "pair" is present, use a singular verb (is, was, has).

Common List:These nouns are composed of two identical or symmetrical parts. They must always end in 's' and follow the "pair" rule.

The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The students of the graduating batch each _______ given a commemorative plaque during the ceremony held in the main auditorium last month.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B)- The blank should be filled with the plural past tense verb "were".

Rule/Concept: Post-Subject "Each" (Plural Agreement) According to the rule marked in your notes, when "each" follows a plural subject (like "Boy and girl" or "The students"), it acts as an appositive and does not change the plural nature of the subject. Therefore, a plural verb is required.

Logic Breakdown:

The Subject: "The students" is a plural subject.

The Position of "Each": Because "each" comes after the plural subject, the verb must stay plural (were).

Tense Consistency: The phrase "last month" indicates the past tense, so "are" is eliminated.

Correct Sentence: The students of the graduating batch each were given a commemorative plaque during the ceremony... last month.
